page: Amazon Web Services m7a.metal-48xl is a bare-metal general-purpose server powered by fourth-generation AMD EPYC 9R14 processors. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this platform delivers 192 dedicated physical cores running at up to 3.7 GHz without simultaneous multithreading (one thread per core). The system is equipped with 768.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, offering a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. Network capability features a baseline throughput of 50 Gbps. The server operates as a diskless metal node without bundled local storage and includes zero GPUs, requiring remote storage solutions for operational persistence.

Benchmark results place the m7a.metal-48xl firmly in the top tier for multi-threaded and high-throughput computing. In compute-intensive evaluations, the instance achieved a stress-ng multi-core score of 592,966.54 and a PassMark CPU score of 144,737.86, both within the top 10% of tested instances. The raw memory bandwidth is equally formidable, registering 657.74 GB/sec on large-block read tests and 314.43 GB/sec on large-block write operations. In operational workloads, the host handled 331.8 million Redis SET operations per second and delivered a static web serving throughput of 113.03 GB/sec, validating exceptional concurrency.

Instruction set features include AVX-512 extensions (AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16), alongside hardware cryptography acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. These vector capabilities support efficient CPU-based artificial intelligence workloads; the host processed 4,464.4 tokens per second on prompt processing for a 135M model and 418.65 tokens per second on a 7B model. However, autoregressive text generation speed drops to average tiers across large language model tests due to the memory latency overhead inherent to purely CPU-based token generation.

Cost efficiency is driven by maximum compute density and the elimination of virtualization hypervisor overhead. Because this is a bare-metal platform without included local disks, organizations trade integrated NVMe storage for dedicated access to 192 physical execution units. The server is ideally matched for enterprise-scale compilation clusters, large in-memory caches, distributed databases, complex simulations, and high-concurrency web microservices.
description: Amazon Web Services m7a.metal-48xl is a general-purpose bare-metal instance powered by 192 dedicated physical cores of AMD EPYC 9R14 processors clocked at 3.7 GHz. Configured with 768.0 GB of DDR5 memory at 5 GHz and 50 Gbps baseline networking, it offers a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio without hypervisor overhead. The hardware features extensive vector support, including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 extensions, but lacks bundled local storage and dedicated GPUs. Benchmarks demonstrate top-tier multi-threaded processing, reflected in a stress-ng multi-core score of 592,966.54, 657.74 GB/sec uncached memory read bandwidth, and 331.8 million Redis SET operations per second. While CPU-based LLM token generation exhibits latency trade-offs compared to accelerators, prompt processing throughput reaches the top 10%. The server is structured for hypervisor deployments, large distributed cache layers, high-volume web serving, large-scale software compilation, and dense compute workloads.
